title: Reverse The Letters, Pin The Rest
statement:
The string s is made of printable ASCII characters. A letter is an English letter, a–z or A–Z.

Return a new string where the letters appear in reverse order, while every other character (digits, punctuation, brackets…) stays at exactly the index it had. Letters keep their case.

examples.why: The letters x, y, z are read back as z, y, x and fill the letter slots. The '-' and '!' do not move.
Letters a, B, c reversed are c, B, a. The '_' sits between 'Z' and 'a' in ASCII but is not a letter.

constraints: s contains printable ASCII characters (codes 33 to 126), no spaces
hints: Where does the first letter end up? Where does the last letter end up?
Put one pointer at each end. Skip over non-letters on each side.
When both pointers sit on letters, swap them and move both inward. Stop when they meet.

explain.intuition:
Reversing means the first letter trades places with the last letter, the second with the second-to-last, and so on. The non-letters are fixed walls that the pairing simply steps over.

So run two pointers inward from both ends on a character array. Each pointer skips non-letters. When both land on letters, swap and move on. Every character is visited once.
steps: Copy s into an array a. Set i = 0, j = n − 1.
While i < j: if a[i] is not a letter, move i right; else if a[j] is not a letter, move j left.
Otherwise swap a[i] and a[j], then move both pointers.
pitfalls: Testing letters with one range from 'A' to 'z'. That range also contains [ \ ] ^ _ `.
Reversing the whole string and then trying to put non-letters back; the indexes get mixed up.
Building the result with repeated string concatenation in a loop in some languages; collect characters in an array instead.

solutions.title: Stack of letters
solutions.idea: Push every letter on a stack, then rebuild the string, popping a letter at each letter slot.

solutions.title: Two pointers
solutions.idea: Walk inward from both ends, skip non-letters, swap letter with letter.

followups: Reverse only the vowels and leave every other character in place.
Reverse the letters inside each word separately, keeping the words in order.
